$comment: Receipts for every number AgentLRay publishes in prose: the README first screen, the hero figure caption, the FAQ and the roadmap. Each claim carries the command that recomputes it from committed artifacts (scripts/claims-receipts.mjs derives the figures from the platform registry, lib/config.js, package.json, the pages workflow, the demo sample log and the test fixtures) or check.manual with the reason no command can. The readme-no-version receipt keeps version-specific installation details in release notes rather than the README. There is no CI claims job: run `node scripts/claims-receipts.mjs <id>` locally for each entry.

claims.claim: AgentLRay supports seven agent log formats — OpenClaw, Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, OMP, DeepSeek Harness and Gemini CLI — registered in one table.
claims.metric: entries in the PLATFORMS registry in lib/platforms/index.js
claims.method: Object.keys(PLATFORMS) is printed directly. The registry is the single source of platform truth: the README compatibility list and the usage-reference format table describe this registry, and every generic surface (session routes, search, watch, insights, prompts, tool audit, OTLP, Markdown/HTML export) resolves platforms through it.

expect.equals: 7 platforms: openclaw, codex, claude-code, omp, dsh, gemini, hermes

claims.claim: Six of the seven platforms are read from JSONL logs; Hermes is the only SQLite-backed one (~/.hermes/state.db).
claims.metric: registry entries carrying a file parser vs entries that read a database
claims.method: The FAQ says 'Six of them store JSONL; Hermes stores SQLite at ~/.hermes/state.db'. The receipt counts registry entries with a parse(filePath) adapter: every platform except hermes has one and is listed through a file-based list/find/collectFiles; hermes has parse: null and is served by getHermesSession against the SQLite state.db.

claims.claim: Both READMEs enumerate the registered platforms; the usage reference has one Supported Log Formats row per platform.
claims.metric: registry labels found in each README, and data rows in the Supported Log Formats table
claims.method: Look up PLATFORMS[].label in both READMEs; count the table under Supported Log Formats in docs/usage.md.

expect.equals: 7/7 labels in README.md (7 format-table rows in docs/usage.md) · 7/7 in README.zh-CN.md

claims.claim: Each platform's default directory agrees with the Default directories table in docs/usage.md.
claims.value: 7/7 default dirs match the usage reference
claims.metric: defaultDir() relative to HOME compared with the usage-reference paths
claims.method: PLATFORMS[id].defaultDir() is resolved relative to HOME and compared with docs/usage.md; README links to that configuration section.
claims.evidence: 平台目录真源在各平台目录声明（lib/platforms/builtin/<id>/dirs.js 与 platforms/<id>/dirs.js），经 @agentlray/shared/config 的 resolveDirs 解析

claims.claim: Both README excerpts show the actual offline report for the committed synthetic OMP walkthrough.
claims.value: 8 historical failures / 7 pending records / 2 events / 1 matching recovery
claims.metric: summary fields from createReport on the committed synthetic OMP log
claims.method: Generate the report using lib/inspect.js and compare all four fields with parsed JSON excerpts in both READMEs. Counts describe log records, not task failures or productivity.

expect.equals: 8 historical failures · 7 pending records · 2 events · 1 matching recovery · complete=true · both README excerpts agree

claims.claim: 727 tests pass on Node's built-in test runner, the count docs/ROADMAP.md records for `npm test`.
claims.metric: passing node:test cases (# tests 727 / # pass 727 / # fail 0)
claims.method: npm test → node --require ./test/setup-env.cjs --test test/*.test.js, and the TAP summary is asserted. The roadmap sentence ('727 tests on Node's built-in runner (`npm test`, 2026-11-19)') is verified by the run, not read back from the prose.

claims.claim: The only GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/pages.yml) builds the demo (VITE_DEMO=1) and deploys it to GitHub Pages; there is no CI test job, so tests, lint and the generated-bundle drift check run locally.
claims.metric: workflow files present, jobs, node-version and whether the demo build runs
claims.method: The workflow directory is listed and pages.yml is parsed: jobs under jobs:, triggers under on:, the branches, node-version and whether a VITE_DEMO=1 demo build is present. The README and usage reference must not claim a test workflow.

expect.equals: 1 workflow (pages.yml) · 2 job (build, deploy) on Node 22 · demo build: yes · on push, workflow_dispatch of master

claims.claim: A per-turn ledger row carries wall-clock time, tokens summed as input + output + cache read + cache write, cost when the platform reports it, and tool-call and error counts; the strip only appears from two turns on.
claims.value: 240 tok = 120 in + 40 out + 80 cache read; cost shown only when reported
claims.metric: the row fields built from two committed fixtures that differ in exactly those columns
claims.method: buildTurnLedger (frontend/src/lib/pure.ts, transformed with the frontend's esbuild) over the dsh fixture (test/fixtures/home/.dsh/sessions/--fixtures-project-delta--/dsh-fixture-session-0001/session.jsonl) and the omp fixture: the dsh turn totals 240 tokens only when its 80 cache-read tokens are counted, and its cost column stays hidden because no cost is reported, while the omp turn reports $0.0054 and one tool error. The two-turn display gate and the sort keys live in frontend/src/views/sessions/TurnLedger.tsx.

expect.equals: dsh: 1 row, 240 tok = 120 in + 40 out + 80 cache read + 0 cache write, cost not reported, 1 tool call, 0 errors · omp: 1 row, 300 tok = 220 in + 80 out + 0 cache read + 0 cache write, cost $0.0054 reported, 1 tool call, 1 error

claims.claim: The published install command is `npx @bowenluo718/agent-lray`, and the package exposes that launcher under two bin names.
claims.metric: package.json name and bin keys vs the README install block
claims.method: The name and the bin keys are read from package.json, and README.md must still carry the `npx <name>` line, so the documented command cannot drift from the published package name.

expect.equals: @bowenluo718/agent-lray · bins: agentlray, agent-lray · README.md npx line present

claims.claim: The server's default port is 3800, the http://localhost:3800 the README tells you to open, and the launcher can override it with --port/--host.
claims.metric: the PORT fallback in server.js and the README's localhost URL
claims.method: `const PORT = process.env.PORT || 3800` is matched in server.js, README.md must contain http://localhost:3800, and bin/agentlray.js must still parse --port and --host.

expect.equals: 3800 · README.md states http://localhost:3800: yes · launcher --port/--host: yes

claims.claim: The package requires Node.js ≥ 22.13 — the floor the README badge and the 'When NOT to use it' section both state.
claims.metric: package.json engines.node vs the README badge and prose
claims.method: engines.node is read from package.json, and README.md must contain both the badge text `Node.js-22.13+` and the prose `≥ 22.13`.

claims.claim: Reading compressed DeepSeek Harness logs requires Node.js ≥ 22.15, because the adapter only decompresses frames when node:zlib exposes zstdDecompressSync.
claims.metric: the Node floor in the shared zstd upgrade message and in the README
claims.method: The floor is parsed out of the message lib/platforms/shared/zstd.js raises for a compressed log, the runtime gate (HAS_NODE_ZSTD = typeof zlib.zstdDecompressSync === 'function') must still guard the decompression path, and README.md must state ≥ 22.15.

expect.equals: 22.15 · shared/zstd.js message "Node.js >= 22.15" + runtime zstd gate: yes · README.md "≥ 22.15": ok

claims.claim: The test suite uses Node's built-in test runner with no test-only dependencies: every require in test/ is a Node builtin, a relative path, the @agentlray/shared alias, or the express runtime dependency used to mount routes in-process.
claims.metric: distinct require() specifiers across test/ by kind
claims.method: Every require('…') in test/*.js is classified; Node builtins (with or without the node: prefix), relative paths, the @agentlray/shared alias and express are accepted, and any other third-party specifier fails the receipt.

expect.equals: 58 files in test/ · 69 distinct requires: 16 node builtins, 50 relative, 2 shared alias, 0 test-only third-party

claims.claim: The README publishes no version number of its own — the npm release badge is the only version shown — so no committed prose can go stale against the registry.
claims.metric: semver-looking strings in README.md, excluding the 127.0.0.1 in the host example
claims.method: README.md is scanned for standalone x.y.z tokens (not part of an IP address). Version-specific installation instructions belong to release notes; this receipt does not assert registry availability.

claims.claim: On one previously studied frozen real Codex snapshot, AgentLRay and an independent native-record parser agree on 36 background-process chains and three preselected forensic questions; 28 recorded successes and eight last-recorded running states.
claims.value: 4,333,237 bytes / 771 records / 36 matching chains / 3 matching answers
claims.metric: Structural association agreement on one private snapshot, not population accuracy, live status or human productivity
claims.method: Choose the largest frozen-byte-count Codex session from the existing five-session audit set before inspecting results. Compare independent JSON/wrapper/ID/order joins with the actual CLI report; reassemble eight source records and verify exact content. Retain the no-matching-nonzero-terminal answer and all uncertainty limits.
claims.repro: Maintainer-local evidence: output/session-forensics/{manifest,results,crosscheck}.json and private frozen input; public method is in docs/session-forensics.md.

check.manual: The source session and full receipts are private, ignored local artifacts, not available to public CI. Locally verified 36/36 lifecycle associations and 3/3 question answers, with 28 success and 8 last-recorded running states. Readers cannot reproduce this sample from the repository. Do not treat arithmetic consistency or document text matching as independent validation of the real log.

claims.claim: The hosted demo at https://bowenluo718.github.io/AgentLRay/ is the real React UI running against frontend/src/demo/fixtures.json — synthetic sample data, no real sessions.
claims.metric: what the deployed site actually serves
claims.method: pages.yml builds frontend/ with VITE_DEMO=1 and deploys frontend/dist, and the fixtures are generated from frontend/demo/sample-logs by scripts/build-demo-fixtures.mjs; whether the deployment currently serves that bundle can only be answered over the network.

check.manual: confirming it means fetching the deployed page and its bundle over the network; the claims job runs offline by design, so the deployed artifact is out of reach here. The committed half — the demo build path and its synthetic source — is what pages.yml and scripts/build-demo-fixtures.mjs describe.
